## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tons of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) add on packages like **ggplot2**

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-build data frame `cars` to play with the plotting:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

plot(cars)

Now with ggplot: First I need to install the package with `install.packages()` \> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot2")` in my quarto document as this will result in me reinstalling the package everytime I render my report.

Every time I want to use a function from a given package I need to load it up with a `library` call:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, columns, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x = speed, y = dist) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_line(color ="red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color ="gold2") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="Speed in MPH",
       y ="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title="Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")


```

## Gene Expression Plot

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2) +
  geom_point(color="firebrick3", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7)

  
```

> Q. How many genes are in this data set?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. How many are upregulated?

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

```{r}
#genes$State == "up"
#genes$State
sum (genes$State == "up")
```

> Q. What percentage of genes are downregulated?

```{r}
n.total <- nrow (genes)
n.down <- sum (genes$State == "down") 

ans <- round(n.down/n.total *100, 2)
ans
```

The percentage of down genes is `r ans` % and that is that ...

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) +
  aes (x = Condition1, y = Condition2, col = State) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha= 0.8)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) +
  aes (x = Condition1, y = Condition2, col = State) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual (values = c("dodgerblue3", "navajowhite2", "red")) +
    labs(x="Control (no drug)",
       y ="Drug Treated",
       title="Gene Expression changes upon drug treament", 
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
```

We can install extra packages with \`install.packages() like them packages for sponebob colors or actually useful ones like **patchwork** for combining plots:

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
      p4

```

```{r}
myplot +
  facet_wrap(~State)
```

## Gapminder

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many entries are there in this data set

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))

```

```{r}
meowplot <- ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes (x = lifeExp, y = gdpPercap, col = continent) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    labs(x="Life Expectancy (years)",
       y ="GDP per Capita ($)",
       title="Life Expectancy based on GDP per Capita")

meowplot
```

```{r}
meowplot +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

Histograms of

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent) +
  geom_histogram()
```

Boxplots of

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, continent,fill = continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
